name: Sable-Arc Concord Overcoat
description:
A long double-breasted overcoat in a heavyweight wool-cashmere blend, cut to fall just below the knee. Notched lapels wide enough to suggest authority without performing it. Six large buttons in a dark horn-composite. Fully lined in silk-weight acetate. The shoulders are structured without being padded — the coat holds its shape whether on a body or on a hanger. Available in charcoal, camel, and a deep midnight navy. Sable-Arc is a Tier 4 label with a flagship on the upper transit corridor, known for making exactly the kind of clothes that corporate directors wear when they want to look like they don't need to try.

This is a coat that says the meeting is already decided before you walk in. It's worn in boardrooms, in the climate-controlled corridors of Spire-adjacent towers, and occasionally by Tier 3 professionals who saved for three months to own one. It has no tech features. It doesn't need any. The fabric and the cut are the technology.
what_it_says: Power that doesn't announce itself. You've been in enough rooms to know that the coat does the work before you speak.
worn_by: Tier 3 aspirational buyers who saved for it
story_hooks: Sable-Arc's head of design has been quietly embedding a single thread of a proprietary dye in each coat's lining — invisible to the naked eye, readable under specific UV frequencies. The company claims it's anti-counterfeit. It is also a tracking marker.

A Tier 3 paralegal who scrimped to buy a secondhand Concord overcoat has been using it to move through Tier 4 spaces unchallenged — until someone who actually knows the label noticed the coat was two seasons old and started asking questions.

Three Concord overcoats were found in an abandoned Tier 2 storage unit, unworn, tags still attached, belonging to a corporate executive who disappeared eight months ago and was never reported missing.
